utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Perhaps we should have the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If I could remind you of the affirmation that you made at the commencement of your evidence which still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Cayley: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Crosland if I could have you turn to tab 33 but initially I have some questions following on from what we were discussing yesterday. Mr. Crosland, you recall yesterday that you were explaining to Their Honours the geographical area of command, what you believe to be the geographical area of command of the headquarters at Malisevo; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In military concerns what is a geographical area controlled by headquarters called?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: An operational area usually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your travels around Kosovo, did you come across any other operational areas of control?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, within the -- when we were looking at the whole problem, we discussed amongst various other people connected with looking for these problems and we drew up rough maps of what we thought were the operational areas, some of which were confirmed by other intelligence sources which we were privy to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these were the operational areas of control of the KLA in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us one other example of the area other than the area of Malisevo, of an operational area of control within Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area around Riznik was under the command the Ramus Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the map there?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not, sir, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's at tab 1.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The areas, Your Honour, I was talking about is the base here just beyond Riznik, and it was thought that this area under Ramus Haradinaj probably went as far as --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you wait a moment, Mr. Crosland, because the map is not on the ELMO. Could we have the map up, please. Thank you. Could you point it out again. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area we're dealing with, Your Honours, is based on Riznik or close to Riznik and it was suggested or thought that perhaps this area of operations would stretch as far as Pec including Decani and down to the area of Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who is the commander of that area?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of that area was Ramus Haradinaj, who I met on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Crosland, what is an order of battle?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's the technical term that military use for the organisation which attempts to show the strength, the numbers of men, the numbers of vehicles, the numbers of weapons, and the ability that particular unit could carry out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- were you ever able to create an OrBat for the KLA in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: An OrBat was created by outside intelligence agencies which I was a little bit skeptical about personally, but this is the fashionable way of looking at intelligence. And it rather produces, in my opinion, a slightly heavier picture than what actually may be on the ground. I went by what we could see on the ground, the various headquarters that I visited as I indicated yesterday, and we went along in parallel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just indicate to Their Honours again the KLA headquarters that you did visit during your travels around Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honours. First of all, the one Ramus Haradinaj is just in the area of Riznik. There was one in the area which is called Jablanica, in this area here. There was another one at Vocnjak. There was one in the Drenica area, in the area here, which is a small village which is not marked. There was a further headquarters east of Kosovska Mitrovica Bajgori. There were further later in the day towards the major town of Podujevo and the villages just in this area here, possibly subservient to Bajgori. In Lapusnik on the main Pristina-Pec road. As we discussed yesterday, the major headquarters or what was perceived to be the major headquarters at Malisevo with a radio station close to the area Crni Lug in the mountains. Another one at Sedlare, and finally down at Crnoljevo on the road from Stimlje, on to Suva Reka, and on to Prizren. There was probably one in the area of Budakovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's all the headquarters that you can remember?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, where was the KLA receiving its supplies from for operations in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I indicated yesterday, Your Honours, most of the supplies were coming through the corridor from the camps based in Tropolja and Bajram Curi through the Albanian border, but roughly between the area here and Vrbenica at the south. That was the initial area. And subsequently later in the year supplies were starting to come through from the southern borders of -- boundary -- bordering Kosovo and Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated yesterday that you were aware of camps in Albania, in Bajram Curi, in Kukes and Tropolja. What was taking place in those camps as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information we received was there was basic military training going on and the forward stationing of resupply of ammunition and clothing and weaponry, which would then be ferried in over the mountains or even smuggled in through Vrbenica, the major international boundary on the border.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to be clear: Training and resupply of which armed force?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can go to the next telegram. I think this was a telegram that was written by you. It's by Landsman; it's by the Deputy Head of Mission. This is a tour that took place on the 9th of July into Kosovo. Were you on this tour?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is with the Kosovo Verification Mission, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you with them?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I -- I -- with the Ambassador and Mr. Slinn, we briefed them at our embassy. We led them into Kosovo, and the British contingent went to Prizren. And then they did their own thing after they had been given a geographical brief by myself and taken around various areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us anything about this report or not?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report on page 2, the UCK controlled the area around Dobro Vodo which is on the main Pec-Pristina road just to the north of the road here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark that with the highlighter.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. Dobro Vodo had been a long-term collection point for people who had been forced out of their houses. The tour then appears to have gone down towards Djakovica, down this major road here, past Rakovina, which is highlighted, and again there was just the usual destroyed and deserted villages in these areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who had destroyed those villages?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had been destroyed by the Serbian security forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anything else in this report?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The record says the UCK was seen in the area of Rudnik, to the north here, on the northern route, which again is quite possible out of the Drenica area. Again very isolated areas up here. And again most of the villages around -- on this road from Mitrovica along to Pec, close to Istok, all the villages there had also suffered major damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By Serbian forces.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again by Serbian forces, yes. Further down the page, the UCK at Crnoljevo, which we looked at in detail yesterday. It's on the road from Stimlje down to Suva Reka, and again as I indicated that was another UCK headquarters. And over the page -- it's called page 5. It's obviously page 3, I think. Wanton damage, and it just reinforces what I've been saying about the amount of damage that was now commonplace throughout Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that damage I think was in the Decani-Pec area, wasn't it, that's referring to, on page 5?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The report states that MUP and JSA forces randomly shooting up homes, houses, businesses and pilfering the contents. VJ also involved in further damage to Crnoljevo. Did you witness Serbian force shooting up houses and pilfering the contents of houses?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, sir. I took a video of this which was then given to General Ojdanic in late July when the Vojska Jugoslavije made the statement that their regular forces, their regular army forces, were not involved in Kosovo, and this video was then produced for the General Staff to prove that this was incorrect. And they were shown using -- or tanks firing their main armament, artillery, and we heard multi-rocket launchers as well, which were fired into the Junik area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any other further comments on that report?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would respectfully draw Your Honours' attention to the last paragraph "Abnormal force," and that is exactly what we've been saying all along is that huge damage had been done. And if I remember rightly, by October a brief I wrote said that over a quarter million people had been disenfranchised from their homes, some had gone to Albania, some had gone to Montenegro, but it was a picture of heavy damage throughout the area of Kosovo itself. Mainly inflicted by the Serbian security forces. There was also some damage done by the KLA as well but not on the same level of destruction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Over the page to the next report which is dated the 30th of July, 1998. What I intend to with these is, to save the interpreters, I'll just read the summaries, and you can make any further comments within the report itself. So this is a situation report of the 28th and 29th of July, 1998. Summary: "Tour taken by UCK north of Orahovac to Malisevo. Released and allowed to travel north to Pec-Lapusnik-Pristina road. Met assault force of SAJ, PJP and VJ lined up for attack on Malisevo. Further combat group include JSO, PJP, and VJ at Cijevo. Ongoing operations in Dulje, Ilaca. Firing all day. Junik under artillery-tank and MOR fire from 1300 onwards. Unanswered questions CLN where is Civpop from Orahovac. Malisevo approximately 30.000. No mention of casualties - possible mass grave in Orahovac. How do Serb authorities explain wanton damage to towns and villages?" Now, first question: Were you on this, sir, particular tour?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I carried out this tour, and it was a return tour from Orahovac going north into the area of Malisevo which we'd been -- we'd been detained in as we discussed yesterday. This time they were obviously aware that a heavy force of Serbian assault forces which you described were on the Lapusnik and just at the Kijevo crossing point ready to come and assault Malisevo, and that assault took place once we got out of the area, but by which time most people had left Malisevo and just massive damage was done to the approach -- on the approach roads to Malisevo. All the villages was destroyed, and some of the area around Malisevo was destroyed although not the area around the headquarters which was left. It was subsequent to this I then took the troika group back down to Malisevo to show them where the UCK had been. And that produced a whole mass of refugees that then left Malisevo and went down into what we call the Pagarushe valley area which is just this area here north of Suva Reka which contain at one stage about 40 to 50.000 refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any further comments, Mr. Crosland, on that report?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. The area around Blace was, as I described yesterday, a Vojska Jugoslavije emplacement from which their artillery was able to support the operations around the whole of this area and from which heavy artillery fire was seen and videoed throughout the months of July, August, and September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think we can go to the next report. This is a report from the Pec military department to the Pristina military district command. STG, derogatory for Albanian terrorist group activities against MUP Ministry of Interior members: "STGs from the village of Junik are offering strong resistance to MUP forces. Part of the village of Junik has been mopped up - the mopping-up operation continues. VJ Yugoslav army forces are helping MUP forces in this and three tanks from the Pec garrison have been engaged. We have no information on the outcome of the fighting." Paragraph 2: "STG activities against VJ members and facilities, conscripts and the civilian population: "VJ forces operating with MUP forces around the villages of Iglarevo and Junik continue mopping up the area around the villages of Iglarevo and Kijevo, as well as Junik itself, where strong STG forces are still offering fierce resistance." Now, simply upon the -- regarding the events referred to in this report, were you aware of these events at the end of July in the Junik area?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. And as I had mentioned just recently, we'd already made the point to Vojska Jugoslavije General Staff that the VJ was involved in operations, and here you've got confirmation from themselves that they were actually involved, although outwardly they were saying they were not. And that's in the fighting around Junik which, as we described yesterday, had been going on for the past three months and is still going on at the end of July. The second point I would like is I was present at the village of Iglarevo which I'll mark on the map for you here, which is just beyond Dobro Vodo area, and we were present when the security forces -- Serbian security forces moved into this village and literally kicked the doors down, burnt the houses and abducted the villagers who were still in these houses. These were a farming community who had remained there in order to try to farm their areas but were engaged by the Serbian security forces as a supposed threat to their operations along the main Pristina, Klina, and Pec road. And there was a systematic destroying of all villages along these roads for that reason, that they offered hiding places for the KLA to attack from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go to the next report. This is the command of the 15th Armoured Brigade. Can you tell the Judges where the 15th Armoured Brigade was based?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, the 15th Armoured Brigade was based in Pristina, on the outskirts of Pristina. We visited this on several occasions before these operations took place. And again I think just reinforces the fact that they were involved, as it says in various paragraphs, with the MUP forces and is further evidence that there was collusion between the Vojska Jugoslavije and the MUP formations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in paragraph 4 previous operations by MUP and VJ units were carried out with the approval and knowledge of Joint Command. Is that the paragraph you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just in terms of paragraph 1, and I won't read out all of the villages, but it is referring to operations around Komorane, Lapusnik, and Kijevo between 25 July and 6 August, 1998. Were you aware of those operations taking place during those dates?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were, Your Honours. I mean, the area we're dealing with extends from Lapusnik here in the north, down to Malisevo, and along to Blace, and Dulje. And this was the central area which is high ground in this area here and was of tactical and strategic importance to the Serbs. And they systematically cleared this whole area, and all the villages along here were more or less flattened by Serbian security forces during this time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go to the report of the 27th of August, 1998. And again I'll read the summary at the beginning. "25 August 1998 ongoing MUP/VJ operations in Stimlje, Dulje, Blace and south from Komorane, towards Sedlare. Heavy artillery and direct fire heard. No access allowed south to Malisevo. UCK appear to be backfilling into old areas. "26 August 1998 gained access through Junik under MUP control and toured south through cordon sanitaire Ponosevac to Djakovica. This area under VJ control but relaxed. Tour took HMA and guest to Josanica and viewed examples of damage to homesteads. Token UCK VCP stopped tour at Brocnja to make impression of UCK-controlled area. Wanton damage and fresh burning of houses continues. Forecast MUP/VJ continue aggressive operations. Damage and humanitarian problem continues to escalate." Now, Mr. Crosland, apart from the mention of Junik again, this is actually referring to the same area that we were referring to with the last tab, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours. And it's really the start of the Serbian security forces attempting to reassert their control over the area which up until then, as we discussed yesterday, three of the four main routes had been blocked by the KLA, and we're now starting to see, if you will, the counter-offensive by the Serbian security forces to clear these areas and attempt to regain control. The area we described is still in the area of Lapusnik, Malisevo, Blace. The operations around Junik are still continuing. And then we then took our ambassador up to Josanica and Vocnjak which is where the KLA had headquarters. And I was to show him that the KLA were organised in a looser way but did have headquarters in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do mention again fresh burning of houses. Do you recall where that was?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this was, as I've said many times, a daily occurrence, and every time we toured around the area the area would be covered in smoke from burning fields, houses, petrol stations, grain stores. Whatever part of the infrastructure the Serbs could get hold of they would then try and destroy in order to ethnically cleanse the area of the Kosovo Albanians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go to the next report dated the 10th of September of 1998. And again I'll read the summary: "Potential gravesite two kilometres south-east of Riznik, 8 to 12 bodies seen. Serbs claim 40, because 40 other people are missing. Chinese rounds found in the area which would indicate UCK responsibility. Autopsy to follow." Paragraph 2: "IDP concentration between 5 and 15.000 people seen moving south, possibly going to re-inhabit wrecked villages of Suva Reka. Komorane to Sedlare, all villages heavily destroyed. Civilian population returning slowly. Tour spoke to people who indicated that only 25 had returned and they were short of food and materials to rebuild." Mr. Crosland, could you please point out for us again the village of Riznik?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honours. We were contacted by the Serbian security forces - we were based in Djakovica at the time - and we were taken under MUP escort up to Prilep and then we turned right into Riznik and then we drove into the area about where I'm pointing now. Another five kilometres north of Riznik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you find when you got there?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the way there, there was ongoing operations of tanks, armoured personnel vehicles, the cutting edge of the JSO, the SAJ were clearing for the second or third time at least the villages of Riznik and Prilep which were heavily damage. Prilep was more or less flattened to about a foot level. These operations were still going on. Hayricks were being burnt, and general destruction of the infrastructure was continuing as we drove past. We then arrived at what was called a potential gravesite, and there were six to eight bodies lying in a monsoon-type drain of about three to five metres deep. I in fact picked up these rounds which had Chinese origin. Potentially this would indicate the KLA had committed this particular crime. However, we were not able to properly identify who these unfortunate people were. I estimated they'd been possibly in the drain between a week and a month, but it's very difficult to know when people are lying in water. As a follow-up to this I took our ambassador and Lord Ashdown to this site, and also the deputy Prime Minister of Serbia, Milutinovic, came down and later -- at a later date. So it is -- unless it was a very clever ruse by the Serbian security authorities to muddle this up, it does look that possibly this was a KLA atrocity, and the comment was that there were still 40 other Serbs or more missing, and they were being held we had indications in the area of Jablanica, in this area here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to be clear: What was the ethnicity of the murdered individuals in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, Your Honours, it would be impossible to tell because we couldn't go down into the water to look at these unfortunates and so they could have been anyone. But the evidence would tend to favour that perhaps for once the Serbs were telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could go -- unless you have any other comments on that, I think that covers --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just respectfully draw Your Honours' attention to paragraph 7. This was a report from the Kosovo Verification Mission about the outlined figures of 171.000, and this gives you some idea of the destruction that had gone on and the mass movement of population that was now starting to take place. A lot of these, as I said earlier, between 40 and 50.000, were in the Pagarushe valley area to the north-west of this area of Suva Reka, where I'm pointing now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here you're referring to displaced persons.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go over the page to the report of the 6th of November of 1998. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Again I'll just read the summary: "Mutual request to discuss rapidly deteriorating security situation in Kosovo, also activities of UCK/KLA, re-engagement of MUP, lack of control, cross-border in Albania, visit by General Perisic units in Kosovo, 4 to 6 November 1998, DA suggested change of tactics is necessary." What is this referring to, this summary?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this refers to a meeting that I was requested by Colonel General Dimitrijevic who was head of counter-intelligence to myself to discuss what was going on in Kosovo, because whilst as I mentioned earlier in the end of August, September the Kosovo -- the Serbian security forces had April period to have seized and made what I would call a tactical strike against the KLA who were at that time disorganised and perhaps on the back foot, there were already worrying indications that stronger resupply to the KLA was coming in from Albania. And whilst the Serbs may have had a tactical advantage, they certainly didn't have the strategic capability of finishing off the KLA. And this is really what General Dimitrijevic is referring to. Because as I mentioned many occasions yesterday -- in yesterday's session, no one side really retained control for more than a passing couple of days or so before the other side then took control back again, and these rings went round and round in ever-decreasing circles. General Perisic, who is chief of the General Staff, went on a morale-raising visit to the VJ troops in Kosovo, who at this stage had thought they'd had the KLA on the back foot, but this was, as we might see later on, to change when the resupply started to come back in, and then NATO pressure was applied to the state of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Dimitrijevic the destruction of the infrastructure and the housing in Kosovo that you had seen taking place?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, Your Honours. And in paragraph 5 he does admit that the VJ had overstepped the mark in the summer offensive, but this had been because the VJ had to step in order to salvage the inefficiency of the MUP. Well, I think that's a moot point as we've discussed. The destruction was -- been going on mainly by the MUP in this particular case, but the direct and indirect fire the artillery and tank fire was coming from Vojska Jugoslavije formations. Again, I would respectfully draw your attention to paragraph 6 that there was in General Dimitrijevic's opinion continued lack of responsibility by Albania to in any way police or control their border. And this is one of the old tales of woe that came from the Vojska Jugoslavije, and with a huge amount of reason, as we've discussed already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on to the next DipTel, which is dated the 6th of November of 1998. Paragraph 4, which I'll read: "Serb and Albanian sources present different pictures of a series of small-scale incidents. The overall impression is that the UCK are assuming control of roads in several areas but that both sides are trying at this stage to avoid major provocations. Shots apparently from the UCK were heard in the Cicavica mountain area of Drenica, the scene of the final major conflict of the summer. In a separate incident, armed Albanians stopped a bus on the Pristina to Kosovska Mitrovica road. They questioned two Serbs; one soldier, the other a policeman. The soldier was subsequently released, but the policeman's whereabouts are unknown. Meanwhile, the two Tanjug journalists remain in the custody of the UCK. The Belgrade media, both state controlled and independent, continues to give prominence to their story." Now, where at this time in Kosovo were the KLA beginning to assume control of roads?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would respectfully draw your attention to paragraph 6, and this was the time that Mr. Holbrooke and I'm right in saying that NATO had issued an ActOrd on the state of Yugoslavia. Therefore, the state of Yugoslavia was under intense pressure to withdraw its forces which they did, the three battle groups, and I and one other person was present when these formations withdrew. The advice that I gave to higher authority, both at London and in "Shape" was that if the Vojska Jugoslavije withdrew from these positions, the KLA would backfill into them unless we replaced them with some kind of force. To be fair to the Serbs, they did withdraw as ordered back to their barracks in -- back to Prizren, back to Urosevac, and back into Pristina. And true to form, the KLA backfilled into some of the positions as we've heard, and shots were fired from the Cicavica mountains, which are the mountains overlooking the valley that runs from Pristina to Kosovska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when it's referring to the UCK human control of roads, that's what it's referring to, what you've just stated?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it also referred to incidents where armed Albanians stopped a bus on the Pristina to Kosovska Mitrovica road and the questioning of two Serbs, a soldier and a police officer, and the disappearance of the policeman. Do you recall that event?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honour. And the Serbs were quite naturally very irate that in what they considered to be their heartland just north of Pristina between Pristina and Mitrovica they had interference. On the western side here --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you pull the map across so that --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, if I might. I appreciate that in Mr. Cayley's opening he indicated that he wished to deal with matters in an entire context; however, we have for some period of time been dealing with a date or dates that are outside of the indictment period, and I would for purposes of the record object on the grounds of relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith. At the moment, the Chamber would not interfere, Mr. Cayley, but you will appreciate that there is some validity in the point that's just been made, and we would invite you to consider carefully that area which has some relevance to the issues in this trial and that which goes beyond that and is merely a very general background picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Could I answer the objection?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You've no need, because I've said we're not going to interfere.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Because I believe there is, and I did state in my opening and I can talk to Mr. Guy-Smith about it after the session, I did state it was necessary actually for the purposes of the legal test laid down in Tadic. But I realise you don't want me to get into that argument, but I think it's perfectly reasonable to adduce this evidence. Nevertheless, Your Honour, I will proceed, and I think you will find there's two other reports after this, so I think Mr. Guy-Smith will be satisfied that I haven't gone beyond the boundaries which I should. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I must say that the little that is to follow encouraged the Chamber's view just expressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Where were we? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were discussing the area about Cicavica which I have hopefully explained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. The -- the arrest of the -- the arrest of these individuals from a bus between Pristina and Kosovska Mitrovica. You recall that event?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do indeed, Your Honours. And as I mentioned before, the area we're dealing with is right on the heartland north of Pristina towards Mitrovica along -- on the western side where there were a number of Serbian villages and where the KLA came down from the Cicavica mountains and managed to abduct one person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the two journalists who were taken into custody by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't, Your Honours. By now there were hundreds of journalists in Kosovo who were all attempting to get a story. Some stuck to some of the advice that was given to them that it was a dangerous place to travel around in, others did not. So I'm not -- I'm afraid I can't recall this particular incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we go to the next report, the 16th of November, 1998. And it's purely paragraph 5 that I'm interested in. "One soldier was killed and three seriously injured on 13 November following an UCK ambush on a VJ convoy near Dulje on the Pristina to Prizren road. The VJ Pristina Corps informed DA (who was travelling from Prizren at the time of the incident) as well as representatives of KDOM/KVM and asked DA to see the injured men and the body. On 15 November, also near Dulje, US KDOM reported that a passing VJ column opened fire aiming above their vehicles. Bullivant (KVM spokesman) stated that KVM had sought an explanation from the VJ. In a statement, the VJ denied that the incident had taken place. Separately, VJ sources suggested that the alleged firing was in fact the sound of a vehicle backfiring. I understand that KDOM are now more relaxed about this incident, though Pellnas (head of KVM liaison office in Belgrade) told me this morning that he thought that the VJ had been aiming at the convoy and he expected Walker to raise the issue at his meeting with Milosevic later today." I've read it for completeness, but what interests me in this report is the attack on a VJ convoy near Dulje. Can you indicate where Dulje is on the map?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's on the favourite road we discussed in detail yesterday between Stimlje, Dulje and back to Prizren. I was in Prizren during the day and was travelling back relatively late at night when we were caught up by the Vojska Jugoslavije roughly in this area and asked to turn to Prizren because this incident had taken place where VJ had been killed and other soldiers wounded. I asked the commander there who I knew reasonably well if I could help, and we went to the hospital and viewed the dead soldier and then gave medical help and medicines to their doctor in order to treat the -- I think it was five soldiers who had been lightly wounded in this particular attack. I made a statement, and it was that statement, a joint statement was signed by both the commander at Prizren and myself explaining this particular incident. As regards the KVM, you will see in paragraph, if I may respectfully pass you to paragraph 10, a comment by Seselj indicating that the Serbs did not necessarily trust KVM. I cannot confirm or deny that this event took place, but as I indicated yesterday, the area of Dulje to Crnoljevo and to Stimlje was an extremely dangerous and demanding area, and it may well be that this incident happened post the strike on the Vojska Jugoslavije where they had lost soldiers and one could understand their anger at that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, which incident are you referring to now?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The incident, sir, in paragraph 5 that talks about the US KDOM having been attacked by the -- or opened fire on by the VJ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the final report, if you could go behind tab 42, and I'll read this: "On 20 November, two Serbian policemen both from north-eastern Serbia were killed and four wounded in Prilep near Decani where their car was hit by an anti-tank device. This was followed by automatic rifle fire. There are reports of heavy-handed police responses in the area over the weekend, including beatings and raids on the few remaining houses left intact in Prilep. UCK announced on 22nd November that they had arrested a Serbian policeman and a civilian suspected of looting Albanian villages. They are being held by UCK police organs. Police figures published on 23 November cite 163 UCK attacks between 13 October and 20 November, resulting in the deaths of 14 policemen and the wounding of a further 21. Two VJ soldiers have been killed and two VJ soldiers and one civilian were reported wounded in the same period." Can you point to Prilep, please?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Prilep is this small -- small town on the road between -- between Pec, Decani. Prilep is here and then down to Djakovica. It was, in effect, the quasi-front line along which fighting took place throughout the months that we have described. And Prilep was a MUP defensive position that was regularly attacked on -- on a regular basis primarily from the KLA who were based, as I indicated to you earlier, just east of the village of Riznik, and so both these villages received acute attention. And I stated just earlier Prilep was now down to about 25 centimetres high.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, their vehicle was hit by an anti-tank device. What would that do?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very close to this time, I can't exactly remember the date, but I visited the KLA headquarters here at Riznik, close by Riznik, which is Ramus Haradinaj's area, and they were very keen to show us off a new range of automatic weapons, sniper rifles, and Panzerfaust, which were anti-tank weapons, sniper rifles which had just arrived on the latest resupply from Albania through the -- the old corridor I mentioned many times down Decani down to Tropolja. They also had on this visit obviously received a lot more clothing because they were in much more regular combat clothing and all wearing a similar natured dress, indicating, as I say, the resupply had got through. And if I may respectfully remind you, we're now dealing with, in paragraph 3 the time when Mr. Holbrooke was in Yugoslavia attempting to draw this particular conflict together. So the Serbs were very much under pressure, and the KLA and Albanian authorities were exploiting this pressure that the Serbs were under.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The figures quoted of 163 UCK attacks, can you make any comment on that, during that time period from the 13th of October to the 20th of November?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This number would not be disproportionate, but it would include major events like the anti-tank -- killing of the policeman with the anti-tank weapon to very minor offences. So stated as 163, there may well have been a hundred serious cases and perhaps 63 not so serious cases, but that's the nature when you start playing with figures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Just some final questions for you to clarify what we were talking about in Malisevo. Did you ever meet a KLA commander quality Fatmir Limaj?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the code name was Celiku, then yes. But the problem in these early days, Your Honours, was that although you asked for names, you were given various code names or synonyms as and when. So I can't specifically say that he was the person I met because they were still acting then under in -- in a very tight way for their own security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the individual that you met in Malisevo, did he speak to you at all about his area of command and the troops that were under his control at that time?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in so many words, no. But as I attempted to indicate, we discussed various towns -- or these villages around the area and he obviously knew of them, and one could draw from that, I think, a reasonable conclusion that these areas were within his tactical operational area. But as I said, Your Honours, it's very difficult to draw together a significant military OrBat with a formation that is running around the countryside attempt -- being chased by a significantly numerically superior force, and therefore they had learnt their lesson in the very first days in the Drenica --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose they - sorry - just for the record.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, the Kosovo Liberation Army, that if they stood and fought in an area that was geographically advantageous to the Serbian forces who were mobile and had weapons able to fire long distances, then they were liable to suffer very severe casualties. So, yes, there was an organisation, there was a command structure, and there were headquarters scattered throughout the province of Kosovo as I hopefully have indicated to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I don't have any further questions for the witness and I can offer him for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Mansfield. Cross-examined by Mr. Mansfield:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Crosland, I represent somebody called Fatmir Limaj. Today appears to be the very first time that there has been any indication from you, is this right, about the possibility of meeting somebody by that name? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. It's the first time I've been specifically asked that particular question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it? The first time you've been asked that question?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I'm aware, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how did you know, therefore, that it might relate to the name Celiku?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because in one of my reports written during the time when I was in Kosovo, this connection came up by other intelligence agencies to which I was privy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, where is that report?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I don't know. These reports are not my property. They are property of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you write the report and under what title was it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I'm attempting to explain to you, sir, the report was one -- I wrote about 85 reports, plus sending verbal reports on secure means back to London. Those reports are the property of the Ministry of Defence, and I have now retired from the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I do appreciate the difficulty. See, I want to ask you, we don't have that report, as far as I'm aware, did you indicate in that report or reports that you had met somebody called Fatmir Limaj?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I, sir, did not know that particular name, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I can be clear: There is no report anywhere in existence, let alone the ones produced here, suggesting that you'd ever met anyone called Fatmir Limaj; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That particular name, sir, was not familiar to me until other agencies said that these two might be linked together, and that is clear as I can make it, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What other agencies?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are other intelligence agencies which I dealt with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What other intelligence agencies did you deal with?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Agencies linked to the Ministry of Defence, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Which ones?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I'm entitled to tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, for reasons that are linked very much to an alleged incident in this case that's relevant to the period on the indictment, I do ask that we know at least the names of the agencies.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: -- as Mr. Mansfield knows, a very sensitive area, and I would ask for an adjournment so I can speak to the Ministry of Defence legal advisor on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: How long?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Five minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will adjourn temporarily. --- Break taken at 10.05 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps it might be appropriate -- I don't want to waste any time -- any more time than is necessary on of this. We'll make a mountain out of a molehill, but if I could address you in private session, and perhaps it would be appropriate out of earshot of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. I'm afraid I must ask you if you would leave the court, and I can indicate that there will be a break after these submissions, the first morning break, so you can expect, I'd think, something toward half an hour before you will come back.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cayley. Private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will now adjourn and resume just before the hour. --- Break taken at 10.37 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, just two very minor matters following on from the discussion before the adjournment. If the -- if Your Honour would be so good as to explain to the witness - because obviously we can't speak to him - that legal advice has been taken on the issue and secondly whether it be possible to do that line of questioning, if Mr. Mansfield is agreeable, in private session for that short period. I think that would safeguard a lot of concerns that have been expressed by the legal advisor from the MOD to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I understand from Mr. Mansfield's nod that he sees no difficulty with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If I could indicate that the issue raised before you left the courtroom has been for the moment resolved. Your concern was whether you were permitted to disclose the information sought in the question, and no objection is being taken by your ministry we are advised by the Prosecutor to you disclosing the identity of the intelligence services from which you drew that information. I think that will be sufficient for the moment, so, Mr. Mansfield, if you would like to continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, I would ask the questions now but it's necessary to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good. We'll move into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've indicated that in relation to the visit to Malisevo where you may have met a commander, that you did make a written report about that, and you think it's one that has already been referred to. That's what you've just said.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Would you kindly let us know which report it is that contains the details about your visit to Malisevo and meeting the commander?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume it's one of these in here, sir. As I indicated to you earlier, I made reports. I made about 85 visits, I think, to Kosovo during this particular period. Some reports were written. Other reports were sent directly on satellite phone as the incidents unfolded. I thought -- and forgive me if I'm wrong, but I thought we debated this issue in the previous session under Mr. Cayley. Exactly which report I'm not familiar with because I haven't seen them for nearly seven years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Crosland, that's fully understood. These were happenings some years ago now. But before you gave evidence, were you given time to familiarise yourself with the documentation that you do have?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this documentation early yesterday morning, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Please understand I'm not intending this to be a memory test, but you're welcome -- and I'm cut it short. You're welcome to go through it if I have this wrong, but amongst the documents that we've been provided with and which you have gone through in detail, there is no document that narrates in any way or describes the visit to the Malisevo headquarters where you may have met someone by the name of Celiku. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I follow your line of question, sir, yes. I would say -- suggest that tab 34 -- in fact, there were two visits to Malisevo, one where I was detained for an hour and a half to two hours where this gentleman may have been this person we're talking about. That is tab 34.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just indicate the passage in there that you say covers this.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the summary paragraph, sir. And then detail 1 which goes Orahovac, Malisevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you read it carefully, sorry to just interpose for a moment, this one that we're looking at at tab 34 is dated the 30th of July; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's describing what has happened in relation to the 28th and 29th, is it not?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's not actually dealing with, unless there's a mistake, the 1st of July, is it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I indicated to you, sir, this is the second visit, and I haven't found the other report yet or the other mention of it yet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I want to be precise about it. I'm sorry to be careful about this. You're welcome to go back through the documents again if you wish, but there is no document, no report, sitrep, DipTel, however you describe it, indicating a visit to Malisevo on the 1st of July where you met or may have met a commander called Celiku. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I follow what you're saying, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the reason I ask the question is why is there no such report if this occurred in the way you describe?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, you'll have to ask my counsel that because I'm only replying to questions that I've been asked to answer. I'm the guinea pig in the middle here, I'm afraid, without being frivolous about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that because you may not remember, but you would have made a report about the visit on the 1st, if it was the 1st?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made a report -- I know I made a report because it was a very significant meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it was the first time that we had actually been or anyone had been, as far as I know, to this headquarters, which was a major headquarters, and I made very specific comments, one of which, Give me 50 good men and we'll sort this business out tonight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where that report is, sir, I do not know. It's not in my -- in my remit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, as I've said, I'm certainly not trying to test your memory about what now you remember writing. I do make the request through you that if you did make a report, which you think you must have done because it was a significant occasion, that that report is provided to us, whichever agency of the ones you've described presently has it. So I think -- I see that's been acknowledged. I'll move on for the moment. On the basis that there must have been a report, it would be presumably facile of me to ask you now to remember anything else about what you wrote in the report other than the question that you just mentioned about, Give us 50 good men and we'll sort it out today, or tonight or something?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I reported in detail about what I saw in Orahovac up to Malisevo under UCK escort. The numbers I described to you earlier were 150 to 200 people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Men and women.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a certain number of foreigners from the region in this area, both of Dutch nationality, and possibly British, even French, and there was one gentleman from the Middle East.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what you remember writing, is it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember writing that, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. It does not include, therefore, writing that you may have met a commander named Celiku?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall that, sir, in detail, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm under oath as you realise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I appreciate that. I'm going about this carefully. There are reasons to do it carefully. Can I just step back a moment? I'm still dealing with this day. The date of this occasion was put to you by Mr. Cayley. I'm not objecting to the fact that it happened, but do you know when it was that you went?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the 1st of July, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know that because?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: My new warrant officer had just joined the team, and it was a very specific day in his memory as well. Because it was quite a challenging event. As I indicated, they were possibly going to detain us or carry out even more dire threats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'll come to that in a moment. Who was the warrant officer?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was my British warrant officer who was attached to the embassy in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Do you remember his name?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Warrant officer Rob Johnson.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Rob Johnson?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was also with a Dutch warrant officer as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as the date sticks clearly in your mind, I wonder if you could -- I'm not going to take time asking you to look it up if you'd accept it from me, that when you were asked about these matters in more detail in 2004, last year, you made a statement. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I made about three or four statements, so --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. This is the third one.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The one you made last year in July. See it if you wish, but in that statement I give you the paragraph number so it can be checked, in paragraph 13, you indicated that you couldn't be sure of the date. It was June or July. Had it just slipped your mind last year, then?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think quite possibly, yes, because I was not involved in any shape or form. I have since, you know, with this -- with this present session, I have been updated and have remembered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who updated you?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: My counsel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you shown any documents with dates on them?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These documents here, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then we know there isn't a document or a report dated the 1st of July or referring to the 1st of July that you wrote at the time, do you follow, that we have?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a document. But it's not in this bundle of documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you last see that document?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably when I wrote it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you wrote it. So you haven't been shown it just before you gave evidence or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have access to these documents. These are all Ministry of Defence documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, again, assuming for the moment that it was the 1st of July that you went, if you're going to visit what you regarded as possibly a major headquarters of the KLA, you would want to give them advance notice that you're coming, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see why we should do that at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because you might got shot out of the water, if you know the expression, if they don't know who you are and you suddenly appear. It's a risk. You're a military -- you know, personnel with rights to go anywhere you please.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: We -- we --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it would be a matter of sense, would it not, to give advance warning?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, we came under fire on many occasions from both sides, probably all three sides. That was one of the risks that I had to take as the commander of this particular patrol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you would want to reduce the risks, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was no open communications and certainly no communications available to me to either contact the KLA at any time during my --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you decide you wanted to go there?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, when.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were staying in Djakovica. I'd been planning that this was an area that we should look at. There was a rule within my vehicle that if anyone felt unhappy about going into an area which was known to be a dangerous area, that they could object. Neither of the other two people objected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It wasn't an accidental patrol along a road in which you were suddenly, as it were, taken into custody. This was a deliberate decision to go to Malisevo because you wanted to have a look; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly that. That was part --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Part of my job was to try and attempt to find out what was happening on both sides of this particular conflict and --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And all that happened - would this be fair - is that having decided to go there along the route that you described yesterday, once you got near to Malisevo, unsurprisingly you were escorted by members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What then?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we left Orahovac and went -- passed through the Vojska Jugoslavije position on the north edge of the town, around the next corner we came straight into a KLA checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Across the road which had been blocked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were then escorted by these gentlemen there to Malisevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what I was putting to you, that unsurprisingly you were escorted into a KLA stronghold.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I achieved what I wanted to do. Whether they achieved what Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. they wanted is another matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I appreciate your point of view, but what I'm suggesting to you here is that this isn't as though you've been captured on the road to Malisevo. You've come to a roadblock, and you presumably indicated you wanted to go to the headquarters, have you, when you get to the roadblock?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: We don't know that particular time whether the headquarters is there or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you indicate when you get to the roadblock who you are?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you indicate to the people what you want to do?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is not that much discussion. Because it's all done at gunpoint in a very defensive manner by the people concerned who were naturally very jumpy at a blue Discovery which the MUP had tried to use in approaching one of their former checkpoints, and afterwards they told me they very nearly opened fire on us irrespective until they realised who I was. So then I produced my licna karta and my identity card to prove my identity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having been escorted into the building which you later determined was a headquarters, in fact would it be fair to say that the people in the building in fact treated you in a proper and professional manner?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the building they did, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I indicated, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did in --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: My -- my --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those are your words.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you made that statement, so that it's clear to the Tribunal, those words come out of your first statement of the three, which is in May 1999, paragraph 18. You may see it if you wish, but you do not say in that paragraph or make any suggestion that anybody talked about abducting or kidnapping you, do you?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to take your word for it, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you like to see it to make it easier?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm perfectly -- accept your word on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you explain why if in fact a serious threat of abducting you was being discussed you didn't mention it in that description of your attendance on the 1st of July?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think in all fairness there was a lot going on. There was certainly -- I don't speak Albanian. I speak reasonable German and Serbian. There was discussions in probably Albanian, and there was certainly as I indicated this gentleman from the Middle East who was extremely unfriendly to the three of us concerned. And having been around these type of people for quite some time, one was extremely wary of what they may or may not be thinking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I appreciate.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: And as the people in the headquarters were, as I made clear to you, treated us with due respect. Outside people had questioned the validity of our licna kartas, our identity cards and our ability to travel into this area which they claimed was under Albanian control, and I think I've explained this to the Court beforehand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you put in the report at the time anything about a discussion, did you report that there'd been a discussion about abducting you? Did you report that back?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember at the moment, but we -- the vehicle was thoroughly searched.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: And some equipment was left behind, and we came back the following morning to collect it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going to suggest to you that it's not surprising given the history that your vehicle would be searched and you would be asked questions. It's not surprising, is it, given the circumstances occurring in Kosovo at the time?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing was surprising in Kosovo, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Right. Now, I want to deal with the person, the commander. You say you met a commander -- or, rather, you saw a commander. Now, the question you were asked yesterday - and I have the transcript so perhaps you'd just accept it from me for the moment - was this: "Do you have any recollection of what he was called, the commander?" Do you remember that was the question?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I don't know whether you now remember the answer, but may I just read what you said yesterday in answer to that question. "The name Celiku has come up. I'm not completely convinced if that was him or not, and it would be difficult for me to say under oath whether that was the exact name or not. I don't know." Now, that was your answer. Now, you've indicated earlier today that you don't know or you can't recall whether in fact you mentioned the name Celiku in your contemporaneous report. Would it be fair to say that you're not in a position to indicate that if you met a commander or saw one there that that person was Celiku, are you?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a reasonably fair assessment as I've already indicated to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Let alone whether that person is Fatmir Limaj. You certainly can't take the further step, can you?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I indicated that to you this morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask a straightforward question on the back of those answers. Have you ever been asked to identify him from photographs, the person who you met?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a very difficult question to answer, sir, because there may well have been some photographs at that time. I don't -- I cannot honestly recall. Because, I mean, this was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'll make it more specific to make it more straightforward. Have you for the purposes of this these proceedings ever been shown any photographs? In other words, has somebody, an investigator, come along to you and said, "Look, you met a commander. Do you think you recognise him, and have a look at these."

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I may have been shown some photographs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: On one of the occasions, but I cannot recall precisely which.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we have your statements, and none of them indicate that if you saw photographs you were able to pick anybody out. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That may well be a fair comment, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It may be a fair comment. All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once again, if in fact that process has been adopted in this case -- it hasn't. Right. I can't take it further. Now, the person who you met who you thought was a commander, you indicated today that that person -- you were asked the question whether you'd spoken to that person. Now, I would like to be clear insofar as you can be. Did you speak to him or not?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, if I remember correctly, he remained in the background, but as I said earlier, as a controlling influence when sometimes the questions became a bit heated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the reason I ask is that the answer you gave today was that not in so many words, but you indicated there was a discussion about towns and that he knew the area and so on. Are you saying that that was a discussion you had?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We spoke of many things about the area in general, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'd like you to be careful. I appreciate the lapse of time here, because again when you were describing this person and your contact with him in the statement in July last year you said this. It's just one sentence I want to read to you in paragraph 13: "I do not recall Celiku speaking directly to me or any other members of my party." Now, if he didn't speak to you, whoever he was, or your party, he wouldn't have discussed towns or areas with you, would he?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: He may not have done, but the person conducting the interview did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The person conducting the interview where, for the statement or at the --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At the -- at the scene of the incidents in Malisevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Malisevo. So the person in Malisevo conducting the interview was -- are you saying that person was the commander?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult for me to recall exactly who was who, as we've been indicating all along.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: These people -- I can't remember, maybe four or five people in the room plus myself and the Dutch warrant officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I appreciate that as well. And the reason for these questions is a further point. In fact, I want to suggest to you, given your answers, that in fact what you thought was the operational area of control for that particular focal point at Malisevo was not what you were told but only what you thought as a military individual was likely to be that area. Would that be fair?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: At some stage the Ministry of Defence produced a guesstimate of what they thought the areas were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, as I've indicated to you, sir, I put my thoughts together as someone who travelled throughout that area, working on the lines of a person who has been involved with training guerilla forces and training in defence. Now, as I indicated earlier to the Court, whether that was a correct assumption or not I cannot judge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You cannot judge. It may be difficult it place it, but when was the Ministry of Defence guesstimate produced?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't with any exactitude say, sir. It was sometime in the middle of the year if I'm right in saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. It might be for the purposes of this case that when you're talking about the operational area as to when you formed those conclusions in relation to the guesstimate provided. So that's why I asked for the date, roughly speaking. So you seem to believe that the guesstimate was available to you about the middle of the year.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possibly a correct time line, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, as I indicated earlier, I and others had our own ideas, some of which were reasonably similar to the Ministry of Defence. Some were perhaps different. Now, I didn't have access to some of the other agencies that presumably the Ministry of Defence did have access to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I follow that. And the basis for this particular line of questions is this: That yesterday when you were asked about the area under control, your answer was very specific. You said, "I suspect their control," and then you described. And in fact, you said it more than once. "I suspect, as I said," and so on. So what you were making clear yesterday was, if I may put it this way, was that this was an assessment by you based on your experience in the region.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. And I drew some of the lines saying Lapusnik on the north that the road may well have been the boundary. The reason for that is the countryside around there is actually very difficult to cross unless you're in a vehicle and therefore potentially a good place to have a boundary. Now, whether that was true or not, as I indicated yesterday, I could not confirm that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Now, I want to come to an important assessment you did make, and I think you've mentioned it on more than one occasion, not only in statements but also in your evidence in the Milosevic trial, and that is that the strength, if you like, of the KLA at that time was such that with 50 trained soldiers on the other side, they could have been nullified. Was that your view?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Effectively, therefore, what you were saying, in your own assessment, was that the apparent efficacy of the KLA and control has been or was -- sorry, was exaggerated in the minds of others, when in fact on the ground it was fairly thin. I'm putting it in colloquial language. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't necessarily disagree with that, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Right. I give an example. You described the three -- the three roads and how they were blocked and so on. I think at one point you say in one of your narratives of this that just because they were able to interrupt the passage of transport on those three roads by no means meant that they controlled the areas of territory between the three roads, although people assumed that.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.
